system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** The Seller’s “[STANDARD]” labels and efficiency note are not evidence of Buyer agreement. All listed positions remain subject to review. The recommendations below use the AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free baseline; underlying DD documents and the complete SPA have not been provided.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation — one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A higher general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and recovery security; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** individually; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, with only excess recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; thresholds confined to general warranties. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**; the Seller’s combination excludes smaller losses and permanently shifts the first AUD 250,000 to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, effective protective notification and longer, separate periods for other categories. | **Seek 24 months and delete the all-Claims extension**; Buyer needs sufficient post-Completion reporting cycles to identify losses without curtailing distinct remedies. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share general caps and time limits. | Separate fundamental warranties covering authority, ownership, fully paid shares and absence of encumbrances; **100% price cap**, no basket/de minimis and a substantially longer claim period. | **Reject general-regime treatment; seek at least six years**, with execution form and applicable limitation rules checked; defective title can undermine the entire purchase. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of claims for fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation, including conduct attributable to Seller, outside contractual caps, thresholds, time bars and remedial exclusions. | **Insert an overriding fraud carve-out across clauses 9.3, 12 and 20.5**; broad boilerplate must not contractually shield Seller fraud or non-excludable liability. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of data-room contents, references, Accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope, against relevant warranties; a frozen, indexed record and controlled updates. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and require specific, fair disclosure**; document availability alone should not transfer unidentified risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. | No knowledge exclusion; fallback limited to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer personnel, without constructive or adviser-imputed knowledge. | **Delete; tightly narrow only as a negotiated fallback**; a discoverability test would largely defeat warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied by delivery of written consent. No final consent or satisfaction evidence supplied. | A Buyer-benefit condition requiring effective written consent **and satisfaction of clause 11.3 conditions**, without unacceptable amendments or concessions. | **Make full satisfaction a Completion prerequisite, waivable only by Buyer**, with a long-stop termination right; approximately 30% of FY26 revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** remains outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout figure, repayment at Completion and effective discharge of all relevant security and guarantees through an agreed closing mechanism; debt reflected in price adjustments. | **Reject an unsecured post-Completion release promise**; Buyer must receive a debt-free, unencumbered business without paying the debt twice. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional Completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-cost treatment unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonus costs and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, through an agreed adjustment/payment mechanism and residual indemnity. | **Itemise and allocate the full liability before signing**, checking employment conditions and avoiding double counting; omission otherwise leaves Buyer funding Seller’s transaction costs. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, but non-payment is not independently established. | Verify payment and contractual chain of title; require payment evidence and an effective confirmatory assignment covering relevant materials, plus a broader specific indemnity for resulting ownership/use disputes. | **Require title cure at or before Completion and broaden the indemnity beyond the invoice**; payment exposure alone does not capture loss of essential IP rights. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, said not to be material; access, exact scope and notification obligations remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, preserved evidence, access/scope findings, privacy-law assessment and appropriate containment, remediation and notifications; specific protection for pre-Completion incident liabilities. | **Keep open, require investigation deliverables and negotiate a specific indemnity/security**; uncertain access and loss do not establish either a confirmed breach or immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals described as ordinary-course costs. | Assess the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** using DD-008 and DD-011 together, including timing, scope, termination rights, accruals and commercial necessity. | **Do not accept the ordinary-course characterisation without verification**; related commitments may require consent or financial adjustment, but are not automatically debt or leakage. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | General limitations and remedy exclusions extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Separate, expressly coordinated regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, price/debt adjustments and covenant claims, with an overriding fraud exception. | **Redraft the definitions, carve-outs and precedence provisions together**; otherwise broad “all Claims” wording can silently neutralise negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller holding 100% of issued shares. | Independently reconcile issued capital, certificates, corporate records, allotment/transfer history, options and other equity rights; investigate encumbrances and obtain appropriate releases and transfer deliverables. | **Treat the register as a starting point, not completed verification**; it does not alone establish clean beneficial ownership or exclude competing rights. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers tax and IP warranties settled under the general regime. | A separate pre-Completion tax indemnity and tax warranties, appropriately longer survival and separate limits; robust IP ownership, licensing, infringement and developer-assignment warranties, plus Ironquay-specific protection. | **Expressly reopen both categories**, seeking tax survival through relevant assessment periods plus a notification buffer and enhanced IP protection; their risks are not adequately addressed by an 18-month, 20% general regime. |

**Immediate priorities:** resolve Bluefen consent, Riverlark discharge and Ironquay title mechanics; correct the bonus funds flow; investigate the export incident; and prevent blanket disclosure and all-Claims limitations from overriding the negotiated protections.
=== END ADVICE ===
